title: The universal surjective-flat locus for algebraic spaces is open
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $A,C,B$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $p:A\to B$, $q:C\to B$, and $f:A\to C$ satisfy $q\circ f=p$. Flatness, local finite presentation, local finite type, separatedness and universal closedness use the chartwise and topological definitions of [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. A map is closed when its map of point spaces sends closed sets to closed sets. Assume that $p$ is flat, locally of finite presentation and closed, and that $q$ is locally of finite type and closed. Then there is an open subspace $V\subseteq B$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace] such that, for every algebraic space $T$ over $S$ and every $h:T\to B$, the base change $f_T:A\times_BT\to C\times_BT$ is flat and surjective if and only if $h$ factors through $V$. Here surjective means surjective on the point sets of [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

source.place: Tag 05XC (spaces-more-morphisms-lemma-where-surjective-flat), all five hypotheses and arbitrary algebraic-space parameter changes.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-flat-locus-base-change] with $(X,Y,Z)=(A,C,B)$; its three hypotheses are among ours. Let $L\subseteq|A|$ be its open flat locus and put $E=|A|\setminus L$. As $p$ is closed, $p(E)$ is closed. Thus $F_0=|B|\setminus p(E)$ is open. Choose an etale scheme atlas of $B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and apply [lem-a1-space-invariant-open-quotient] to this open subset. It gives an open subspace $F\subseteq B$ with $|F|=F_0$.

source.place: Tag 05XC (lemma-where-surjective-flat), proof; flat-locus construction expanded from Tag 05XB (lemma-where-flat).

proof.text: For any $h:T\to B$, write $a:A\times_BT\to A$. By Step 1 the flat locus of $f_T$ is $a^{-1}(L)$. Hence $f_T$ is flat exactly when no point of $A\times_BT$ projects into $E$ (flatness means flatness at all points, by the chart test). The point-pair surjectivity in [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] shows that such a point exists if and only if some $e\in E$ and $t\in|T|$ satisfy $p(e)=h(t)$: every such pair lifts to a point of the fibre product. Consequently $f_T$ is flat if and only if $h(|T|)\subseteq|F|$. By [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests] this is equivalent to factorization of $h$ through $F$. In particular $f_F:A_F\to C_F$ is flat, where $A_F=A\times_BF$ and $C_F=C\times_BF$.

source.place: Tag 05XC (lemma-where-surjective-flat), proof; flat-locus construction expanded from Tag 05XB (lemma-where-flat).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-lfp-permanence] to $f$ and $q$: $qf=p$ is locally of finite presentation and $q$ is locally of finite type. Thus $f$ is locally of finite presentation. Its base change along $C_F\to C$ is $f_F$: for each test sheaf, a pair consisting of an $A$-section and a $C_F$-section over the same $C$-section is exactly an $A$-section and an $F$-section over the same $B$-section. This is the fibre-product universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The base-change rule of [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] applies to these morphisms, which are representable by algebraic spaces since their sheaf fibre products are algebraic spaces. Hence $f_F$ is locally of finite presentation. Together with its flatness, [lem-sfb-flat-lfp-space-universally-open] implies that $I=f_F(|A_F|)$ is open in $|C_F|$.

source.place: Tag 05XC (lemma-where-surjective-flat), proof; flat-locus construction expanded from Tag 05XB (lemma-where-flat).

proof.text: Let $q_F:C_F\to F$ be the projection. It is closed even though we have assumed only closedness of $q$. Indeed [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests] and [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] identify $|C_F|$ with the open subset $q^{-1}(|F|)$ of $|C|$. Any closed subset of this subspace is $D_0\cap q^{-1}(|F|)$ for some closed $D_0\subseteq|C|$. Its $q_F$-image is $q(D_0)\cap|F|$, closed in $|F|$ because $q$ is closed. In particular $D=|C_F|\setminus I$ is closed and $q_F(D)$ is closed in $|F|$.

source.place: Tag 05XC (lemma-where-surjective-flat), proof; flat-locus construction expanded from Tag 05XB (lemma-where-flat).

proof.text: The subset $V_0=|F|\setminus q_F(D)$ is open in $|F|$, hence in $|B|$, since $F$ is an open subspace [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Apply [lem-a1-space-invariant-open-quotient] to an atlas of $B$ as in Step 1 to obtain an open subspace $V\subseteq B$ with $|V|=V_0$. The inclusion $V\to B$ factors uniquely through $F$ by [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests], since $V_0\subseteq|F|$.

source.place: Tag 05XC (lemma-where-surjective-flat), proof; flat-locus construction expanded from Tag 05XB (lemma-where-flat).

proof.text: For any $g:T\to F$, let $r:C_F\times_FT\to C_F$ and $s:C_F\times_FT\to T$. The morphism $(f_F)_T$ is the base change of $f_F$ along $r$: on every test object both source descriptions are pairs of an $A_F$-section and a $T$-section with the same $F$-section [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The image formula in [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] therefore gives $\operatorname{im}|(f_F)_T|=r^{-1}(I)$. Thus $(f_F)_T$ is surjective if and only if $r^{-1}(D)$ is empty. The same node gives $s(r^{-1}(D))=g^{-1}(q_F(D))$: one inclusion follows by commutativity, while for the other a pair $d\in D,t\in|T|$ with $q_F(d)=g(t)$ lifts to a point of $C_F\times_FT$. Therefore surjectivity is equivalent to $g(|T|)\subseteq V_0$. If this holds, the composite $T\to B$ factors through $V$ by [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests]. Conversely such a factorization has point image in $V_0$; hence the equivalence holds in both directions.

source.place: Tag 05XC (lemma-where-surjective-flat), proof; flat-locus construction expanded from Tag 05XB (lemma-where-flat).

proof.text: Finally let $h:T\to B$ be arbitrary. If $h$ factors through $V$, Step 5 also factors it through $F$, so Step 2 gives flatness of $f_T$, and Step 6 gives surjectivity. Conversely, if $f_T$ is flat and surjective, Step 2 gives its unique factorization $g:T\to F$, and Step 6 then factors $h$ through $V$. Here the maps over $F$ in Step 6 equal the original base changes over $B$: by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], on each test object a pair into $A_F$ and $T$ over $F$ is uniquely a pair into $A$ and $T$ over $B$, since the $F$-section is forced to be the given section composed with $g$. The same applies to $C$, and these identifications commute with $f$. This proves the claimed universal property for arbitrary algebraic spaces $T$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_openSubspace_universal_surjective_flat {S : Scheme.{u}} (A C B : AlgebraicSpace S) (p : A ⟶ B) (q : C ⟶ B) (f : A ⟶ C) (w : f ≫ q = p) (hp_flat : MapIsFlat p) (hp_lfp : MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation p) (hp_closed : ∀ Z : Set (Point A.obj.obj), IsClosed Z → IsClosed {y : Point B.obj.obj | ∃ a : PointRepresentative A.obj.obj, (Quot.mk _ a : Point A.obj.obj) ∈ Z ∧ (Quot.mk _ (a.map p.hom.hom) : Point _) = y}) (hq_lft : MapIsLocally (@LocallyOfFiniteType) q) (hq_closed : ∀ Z : Set (Point C.obj.obj), IsClosed Z → IsClosed {y : Point B.obj.obj | ∃ c : PointRepresentative C.obj.obj, (Quot.mk _ c : Point C.obj.obj) ∈ Z ∧ (Quot.mk _ (c.map q.hom.hom) : Point _) = y}) : ∃ V : OpenSubspace B, ∀ (T : AlgebraicSpace S) (h : T ⟶ B), (MapIsFlat (baseChangeDiagramMap p q f w h) ∧ pointImage (baseChangeDiagramMap p q f w h).hom.hom = Set.univ) ↔ ∃ l : T.obj.obj ⟶ V.val.toFunctor, l ≫ V.val.ι = h.hom.hom
lean.note: The helper constructs the canonical map between sheaf fibre products using their algebraic-space closure theorem; no representability hypothesis is imposed on f. The hypotheses and conclusion are equivalent to the delivered ones (mapPoint sends Quot.mk a to Quot.mk (a.map f)); nothing else changed.
